front: A finch population's mean beak size increases steadily across drought years. Classify the selection and describe the graph change.
why: Classifying directional selection from finch data is a common applied question

front: A mule (horse x donkey) is healthy but sterile. Classify this reproductive barrier precisely.
why: Hybrid sterility as a postzygotic barrier is a common classification

front: Adaptation requires {{c1::preexisting}} heritable variation; environments do not induce the mutations they favor.
why: Selection sorts preexisting variation; mutations are not induced - core Darwinian logic

front: An allele rises in frequency in all ten replicate populations under one condition. Selection or drift?
why: Replicate-population selection vs drift inference is secondary reasoning

front: Antibiotic resistance spreading through a hospital population is an example of {{c1::directional}} selection observed in real time.
why: Restates the antibiotic-resistance natural selection card

front: Apple maggot flies diverging on hawthorn vs apple hosts exemplify {{c1::sympatric speciation in progress via host (habitat) isolation}}.
why: Specific organism example of sympatric speciation; concept card covers it

front: Artificial selection differs from natural selection in that humans:
why: Artificial selection is secondary context

front: Biogeographic evidence: why do oceanic islands host endemic species that resemble the nearest mainland forms?
why: Biogeographic evidence is a minor line of evidence

front: Character displacement: two species differ MORE where their ranges overlap than where they live apart. Why?
why: Character displacement is ecology detail not on the AAMC outline; a passage would define it

front: Coefficient of relatedness: full siblings r = 1/2; first cousins r = {{c1::1/8}}.
why: Coefficient of relatedness values are needed for kin selection questions

front: Contrast allopatric and sympatric speciation.
why: Allopatric vs sympatric speciation appears on nearly every exam

front: Contrast gradualism and punctuated equilibrium.
why: Gradualism vs punctuated equilibrium is a perennial discrete

front: Contrast the reproductive strategies favored in unstable versus saturated environments.
why: r/K selection is secondary ecology content

front: Convergent vs divergent evolution: classify dolphin/shark body forms versus Darwin's finches.
why: Convergent vs divergent evolution is tested on essentially every exam

front: Direct observational evidence of evolution includes {{c1::antibiotic and pesticide resistance evolving within human lifetimes}}.
why: Restates the antibiotic-resistance cards and adds named studies (Grants, Lenski)

front: Distinguish homologous and analogous structures.
why: Homologous vs analogous structures is a foundational every-year distinction

front: Evolutionary fitness is defined by {{c1::relative reproductive success}}, not by survival, size, or strength.
why: Restates the fitness definition card

front: Evolutionary fitness is defined strictly as {{c1::relative reproductive success — allele contribution to the next generation}}.
why: Near-verbatim restatement of the fitness-definition cards

front: Female fireflies respond only to their own species' flash pattern. This prezygotic barrier is {{c1::behavioral isolation}}.
why: Behavioral isolation is a commonly tested prezygotic barrier

front: Frequency-dependent selection means fitness depends on:
why: Frequency-dependent selection maintaining polymorphism is commonly tested

front: Group selection is controversial because:
why: Group selection critique is secondary

front: Hamilton's rule states that altruism is favored when {{c1::$rB > C$}}.
why: Hamilton's rule rB > C is needed for kin selection questions

front: Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium requires all of the following EXCEPT:
why: Hardy-Weinberg assumptions are asked on essentially every exam

front: How can a costly ornament like a peacock's tail be an honest signal of quality?
why: Handicap principle is beyond MCAT scope; cloze twin kept instead

front: How does artificial selection differ mechanistically from natural selection?
why: Restates the artificial vs natural selection card with Darwin history

front: How does phyletic gradualism differ from punctuated equilibrium in what each predicts of the fossil record?
why: Fossil-record predictions elaborate the gradualism vs PE card

front: Hybrid breakdown differs from other postzygotic barriers because {{c1::the F1 is viable and fertile, but F2 or backcross generations fail}}.
why: Hybrid breakdown is a secondary postzygotic subtype

front: If AA leaves 100 offspring and aa leaves 80, then aa has relative fitness $0.8$ and selection coefficient {{c1::$s = 0.2$}}.
why: Relative fitness and selection coefficient calculation is commonly needed

front: Inclusive fitness equals direct fitness from one's own offspring plus {{c1::indirect fitness through relatives' reproduction}}, weighted by relatedness.
why: Restates the inclusive fitness / kin selection card

front: Intersexual vs intrasexual selection: in each, who does the choosing or the competing?
why: Intersexual vs intrasexual selection is a commonly tested distinction

front: Male deer fighting for access to females is {{c1::intrasexual}} selection, while peahen choice of tail displays is intersexual.
why: Example restatement of the intersexual/intrasexual card

front: Mechanical isolation means {{c1::reproductive structures are physically incompatible}} — mismatched genitalia or flower architectures.
why: Mechanical isolation is one of the prezygotic barriers asked in classification

front: Peacock trains persist despite predation costs because sexual selection maximizes {{c1::reproductive success, even at the expense of survival}}.
why: Restates sexual selection opposing survival and the fitness-as-reproduction cards

front: Punctuated equilibrium describes {{c1::long morphological stasis interrupted by rapid speciation events}} in the fossil record.
why: Restates the gradualism/punctuated card and adds Eldredge and Gould names

front: Rapid diversification of a single lineage into many niche-specialized species is {{c1::adaptive radiation}}.
why: Adaptive radiation is a named outline term tested nearly every year

front: Reinforcement predicts that prezygotic barriers become {{c1::stronger in sympatry than in allopatry}}.
why: Reinforcement is beyond MCAT scope; a passage would supply it

front: Relative fitness w and the selection coefficient s are related by {{c1::$s = 1 - w$}}.
why: Restates the relative fitness / selection coefficient card

front: Resistant bacteria often decline once the antibiotic is removed. What does this reveal about fitness?
why: Environment-dependent fitness is a common passage inference

front: Sea urchin species broadcast gametes into the same water, yet hybrids are rare. Which reproductive barrier explains this?
why: Gametic isolation is one of the prezygotic barriers asked in classification

front: Sickle cell in malarial regions is the standard example of which selection mode, and what is its signature?
why: Sickle cell heterozygote advantage / balancing selection is a perennial discrete

front: Speciation without geographic separation is {{c1::sympatric speciation}} — via polyploidy, host or habitat shifts, or strong sexual selection.
why: Sympatric speciation mechanisms are commonly tested

front: Sympatric speciation occurs:
why: Restates the allopatric vs sympatric contrast card

front: The biological species concept defines species by {{c1::reproductive isolation}} — a criterion inapplicable to asexual taxa and fossils.
why: Biological species concept by reproductive isolation is foundational

front: The handicap principle holds that costly ornaments are honest signals because {{c1::only high-quality males can survive while bearing the cost}}.
why: Handicap principle is secondary sexual-selection theory

front: The molecular clock infers divergence times from {{c1::the roughly constant accumulation rate of neutral sequence differences}}.
why: Molecular clock concept is commonly tested

front: The selection mode that produces a bimodal (two-peaked) trait distribution is {{c1::disruptive selection}}.
why: Reading a bimodal distribution as disruptive selection is a common graph question

front: The selection mode whose graph keeps the same mean but narrows the curve is {{c1::stabilizing selection}}.
why: Stabilizing selection is tested every administration

front: The selection mode whose trait-distribution graph shows the peak shifting toward one extreme over generations is {{c1::directional selection}}.
why: Directional selection is tested every administration

front: Two frog species share a pond, but one breeds in early spring and the other in midsummer. Name the barrier type.
why: Temporal isolation is a commonly tested prezygotic barrier

front: Under negative frequency-dependent selection, an allele's fitness {{c1::decreases}} as it becomes common.
why: Restates the frequency-dependent selection card with extra examples

front: Vampire bats share blood with unrelated roostmates who previously fed them. Kin selection or reciprocal altruism?
why: Reciprocal altruism vs kin selection example is secondary

front: Vestigial structures like the whale pelvis argue for evolution because {{c1::they are reduced remnants of functional ancestral structures}}.
why: Vestigial structures as evidence for evolution is commonly tested

front: What are prezygotic vs. postzygotic isolating mechanisms?
why: Pre- vs postzygotic barriers are tested every administration

front: What does fitness mean in evolutionary terms?
why: Fitness as reproductive success is a foundational every-year definition

front: What initiating event does allopatric speciation require?
why: Elaborates the allopatric speciation card

front: What is inclusive fitness / kin selection?
why: Inclusive fitness and kin selection are tested in both Bio and Psych/Soc

front: What is sexual selection?
why: Sexual selection definition is a perennial discrete

front: What long-term advantage does sexual reproduction provide despite its twofold cost?
why: Muller's ratchet and twofold cost are beyond MCAT scope

front: Which selection mode can serve as the first step toward sympatric speciation, and why?
why: Disruptive selection to speciation link is secondary

front: Which type of selection favors individuals at both extremes of a trait distribution?
why: Disruptive selection is tested every administration

front: Why do biologists reject naive group selection explanations such as animals limiting births for the good of the species?
why: Restates the group-selection card

front: Why do ground squirrels give alarm calls that raise their own risk of predation?
why: Alarm-call kin selection example is secondary

front: Why do recessive deleterious alleles persist in populations?
why: Recessive alleles hidden in heterozygotes is core, tested every year

front: Why does haplodiploidy in bees and ants favor sterile worker castes?
why: Haplodiploidy 0.75 relatedness is trivia-grade specificity

front: Why does polyploidy produce essentially instantaneous speciation in plants?
why: Polyploidy as instant sympatric speciation is a common example

front: Why does selection act on phenotypes yet only heritable variation produces evolutionary change?
why: Selection on phenotype, only heritable variation evolves - core principle

front: Why is antibiotic resistance a demonstration of natural selection?
why: Antibiotic resistance as natural selection is commonly tested
